result.summary:
The Blender asset pipeline now runs end to end, from a Python script to the game renderer, and the pilot on VORN's rig works in the real engine. The integrated game still builds and plays: a private build of `#demo=vorn,iska,hard&seed=7` was captured after the shader change, with no page errors and the page size unchanged at 2.5 MB. I kept the earlier partial work that was sound (export_rig.mjs, edlib core/body/sdf/cloth/skin/model) and fixed or finished the rest.

**Delivered, by item:**
1. **Rig export.** `export_rig.mjs` writes `rigs/kael|iska|vorn|pilot.json` in about 7 s. Each file has every bone (parent, bind/zero matrices, length, kind and which bones deform), sockets, weapon grip frames and extents, colliders, springs, cloth panels, proportions, sampled poses and the axes. Re-exporting left kael/iska/vorn byte-identical.
2. **edlib.** I added `bake_object_maps` (object-space normal in game axes, plus AO and albedo-tone mask), `uv_from_grid`, a cheaper level of detail for lamellar (`lod=0`), an `across` option for `weave`, flat lacing stitches, and panel `top` frames in `define_panel`.
3. **Asset format and export.** The exporter now writes a bake stream (u, v, weight) and per-part map names, and fills each vertex's glow from its look. `build_assets.sh <hero|all> [--preview]` regenerates rigs and assets in one go.
4. **Runtime.** New `src/char/assets.js`: `registerAsset`, `getAsset`, `addAsset(kit, ref, { parts, exclude, slotMap, looks, design })`, `assetCloth` (Blender-draped panels become runtime cloth specs), `attachAssetMaps`, `assetTextures`, `assetStats`. The asset decodes once and is shared by both fighters. `tools/build.mjs` gained an `.edm` binary loader, so only targets that import a hero embed it. Designs that don't use assets are untouched.
5. **Shader.** `materials.js` now reads optional baked maps (an object-space normal map in bind space and an AO / curvature / albedo mask) through a per-vertex `bake` attribute. It is still one shared program, and with maps off nothing changes.
6. **Pilot** (lab design in `src/char/asset_pilot.js` + `src/labs/asset.js`). It has:
   - a base body with wrapped forearms and palms, and hands that close around the spear;
   - a crossed-collar robe with brocade trim;
   - a three-panel skirt draped by Blender cloth simulation, its lower part on runtime cloth panels;
   - a sash whose ends ride the front skirt panel;
   - a lacquered lamellar cuirass and left shoulder piece with gold lacing;
   - a conical bamboo hat: a 3.3k-triangle cone whose real plait is baked into maps (about 10k triangles saved);
   - a cloth face wrap, glowing eyes, and a braided queue on four spring bones;
   - the spear at exactly VORN's length.

   Captures (all under `shots/blender/pilot/`) show it next to the kit-built VORN: Blender sheets, an in-engine turntable, bust, silhouette, an arena pair, waist and hands close-ups, and vorn.idle, vorn.walkF and vorn.thunder_pierce at 6 frames each. Deformation at shoulders, elbows, hips and knees looks clean in those frames, and no detached geometry is visible at that scale.
7. **Docs.** `tools/blender/README.md` (running, conventions, binding table, library reference, hero script skeleton, format, budgets, troubleshooting), plus new pipeline sections in CONTRACT.md and `src/char/kit/README.md`.

**Pilot measurements (high tier):**

| | Pilot | Kit VORN | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| Triangles | 48,720 | 58,714 | ≤ 60k |
| Draw calls | 4 | 4 | ≤ 6 |
| `char.update` (median / p90) | 0.6 / 0.9 ms | 0.7 / 0.9 ms | ≤ 1 ms |
| Asset size | 1.41 MB (108 KB of it baked maps) | – | ≤ 2.2 MB |

- **Boot cost:** header decode 1.3 ms, part decode 12 ms, a second character builds in about 38 ms, so roughly 51 ms of asset cost against the 150 ms budget. The first pilot takes 467 ms, which I believe is mostly the kit's one-time texture-set generation for the looks it uses rather than the asset itself; I did not measure that split.
- **Dispose:** three create/dispose cycles leave GPU geometries, textures and programs unchanged.
- **Low tier:** 48.7k triangles, `char.update` 0.4 ms.
- **Page size:** the game is unchanged at 2.5 MB; the asset lab page is 3.2 MB.

**Bugs fixed along the way:**
- The skirt drape lost its shape: the drape collider's normals pointed inward, so the skirt fell inside the trousers.
- The skirt showed its lining on the outside.
- The spear blade was read after its object had been joined away.
- The lamellar was 36k triangles (now 15k).
- Images were upside down at load (`flipY`).
- A missing glow attribute zeroed the look's glow constants.
issues: The game itself (`actor.js`) calls `design.attach(char)` without the quality tier, so `attachAssetMaps` cannot skip the baked maps on the low tier there. It works in the lab, which passes `ctx.quality`. The fix is a small change in a read-only file: pass `ctx.quality` as a second argument.

Baked maps are found in the merged slot mesh by matching each vertex's exact bind position and normal, because `build.js` (read-only) drops extra vertex attributes. This works, but it allows only one baked map set per material slot. A rig-team change letting kit pieces carry an extra attribute would make it simpler.

The pilot's hands are visibly blocky in close-ups (fused-looking fingers, skin reads pink-orange in the studio light). The palm wraps hide much of it, and at fight distance they read fine. The shared `ed.hand()` would benefit from a sculpt pass before the hero artists rely on it.
The robe's upper silk and face wrap are near-black under the lab lights. The colours follow the art direction but are worth retuning per hero with `addAsset` look overrides.

Lamellar, embroidery and lacing are still real geometry with vertex data (lamellar `lod=0`, about 15k triangles). Only the hat weave uses baked maps so far. Moving the lacing to maps could save another 3-5k triangles.

The first character built in a page costs about 467 ms, which I believe is mostly the kit's one-time texture-set generation (shared with the kit-built heroes) rather than the asset; the asset's own decode and build is about 51 ms. I did not measure that split.

Seams added by decimation can leave a vertex with 5-6 weight influences in Blender; the exporter trims to 4 and renormalises. Run `limit_normalize` after `decimate_to` if exact parity between the Blender preview and the engine matters.
`rigqa` was not re-run because the rig runtime was not touched. The art lab (vorn and the reference outfit) and a game demo were re-captured after the shader change with no page errors.

result.summary:
Iska (설리화) now wears a cleaned-up Blender asset that works in the game, within budget: 59,390 triangles, 4 draw calls, 1.58 MB. A predecessor had already built and integrated the model, but it was over the triangle budget and had visible defects. Those defects are fixed and checked in the art lab, in a new lab of my own (`src/labs/iska_asset.js`) and in a private game build. That build is 7.5 MB, under the 12 MB page limit.

**Defects found and fixed in `tools/blender/heroes/iska.py`:**
- **White robe torn and patched with indigo.** The robe, sleeves, sash, legs, mask and fittings were decimated after being given thickness. That pushed the indigo lining through the outside and tore the hems. Decimation now happens on the sheet before thickening, and part sizes are set by the generators.
- **Bad bending in poses.** Garments copied their skin weights from the body after it had been culled, so they took weights from whatever skin was left (the neck, stray patches). They now copy from an unculled copy of the body.
- **Skin poking through cloth.** Torso, arm, leg and foot skin, which is always under cloth, is now deleted; only the head, neck and hands remain.
- **Jagged edge at the V neckline.** The lapel bands now straddle the cut edge and cover it.
- **Robe showing through the sash.** The robe's blousing ended at the sash, which put the robe outside it. Blousing now stops above the sash, the robe under the sash is removed, and around the sash the robe moves with the sash's hip and spine weights.
- **Lumpy face veil.** The veil now hangs as a sheer gauze curtain from behind the mask, falls straight past the chin and is drawn back toward the neck; the face shows faintly through it.
- **Knee coming through the front skirt panels in deep stances.** In `design.js` the panels now follow the thigh more closely (86%, was 62%) and their springs are stiffer, so they ride the thigh like an apron. Bones, rest poses, sockets, weapons and colliders are untouched.
- **Triangle budget.** 60,623 → 59,390. Robe and sleeve surface noise is also softer.

**Baked maps:** the silver mask now has a baked normal map and an AO / tone map (75 KB), made from a detailed copy with border grooves, frost patterns off the eye slits and a hammered surface. The first bake came out nearly black because the detailed copy had no base colour set; that is fixed, and it now reads as engraved silver.

**Silhouette:** I kept the silver half-mask with the long bound tail and hairpin rather than the bamboo hat. In the black line-up she is clearly distinct from VORN (spear) and KAEL (saber). In the pirouette and backflip the sleeves end above the wrists and never cover the crescents.

**Motion review:** idle, walk, dash, guard, light, heavy pirouette, skill, hit, knockdown and the ultimate opener, 6 frames each in a private game build of `#training=iska,vorn`. Close-ups of the pirouette, backflip, hit and fall come from the new lab. Shoulders, elbows, hips and knees bend cleanly at those camera distances.

**Numbers (high tier):**

| | Iska | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| Triangles | 59,390 | ≤ 60k |
| Draw calls | 4 | ≤ 6 |
| Asset size | 1.58 MB (1.51 MB geometry + 75 KB maps) | ≤ 2.2 MB |
| Boot decode | 1.1 ms header + 22.6 ms parts; a second Iska builds in 37 ms | ≤ 150 ms |
| First Iska | 504 ms | — |
| `char.update` median / p90 | idle 0.5 / 0.9 ms, walk 0.4 / 0.8 ms, pirouette 0.4 / 0.5 ms | ≤ 1.0 ms |
| Low tier | maps skipped, 0.3 / 0.5 ms | — |
| Dispose, 3 cycles | geometries, textures and programs unchanged (12 / 22 / 17) | clean |

The 504 ms for the first Iska likely includes the kit's one-time texture generation (the pilot report gave the same reason); I didn't measure the split.

The hero README now opens with a section on the asset: parts, materials, glow channels, cloth and springs, these numbers, how to rebuild and the pipeline lessons. The old kit-build notes are kept below it.
issues: Hands read fine at game distance, but up close the hand under the leather palm wrap is still the stock body hand and looks blocky.
In deep stances the indigo lining of the back skirt panels shows through the slit beside the white front panel. This is plausible for a split skirt, but it is not verified as intentional.
Only the mask has baked maps. The blades, bracers and robe rely on per-vertex data (AO, curvature, glow). A gear-slot atlas covering the bracers and blades would be the next step.
The art lab's arena line-up shows Kael's older kit build, not his asset; his artist is still mid-work. My own lab's silhouette line-up uses the current designs.
The game clip review script `clips.mjs` lives only in my scratch directory. It is outside my owned files, so it is not committed.

`export_rig.mjs` rewrites every rig file, so `tools/blender/rigs/kael.json` was regenerated from Kael's design as it currently is on disk. Kael's artist owns it and should re-run the export when they finish.

Candidate shared helpers for edlib (not moved; edlib is shared): `orient_out`, `thick` with sheet-level decimation, `sleeve_shell`, `head_grid`, and a 'falling curtain' veil grid. A related lesson: `bake_object_maps` needs `ed_col` set on the high-poly, or the albedo channel comes out at about half.

Low tier: 0.3 / 0.5 ms with maps skipped. Dispose over 3 cycles is clean (12 / 22 / 17 geometries / textures / programs before and after). The private game build is 7.5 MB, under 12 MB.

result.summary:
KAEL (염무강) is built from code in Blender and plays in the real game. The asset is 59,621 triangles in 4 draw calls and 2.12 MB, and char.update stays at 0.3–0.4 ms. The mask and pauldron were rebuilt; they had been rendering as broken chrome until I found and fixed a mesher bug.

An earlier session had already got the whole chain working (scripts, asset, design.js integration) and its files survived the reboot, so I continued from them. The rig data in design.js is unchanged: proportions, bones, sockets, colliders, and the saber's length, grips and sockets (the predecessor added head and neck colliders for the cloth and mane; no clip reads them).

**What I changed:**
- **Demon half-mask (귀면):** remodelled because the old one was lumpy. The shell is now cut into flat planes with bevelled edges. Heavy scowling brows with a flat top and an undercut, flame tufts at the outer ends, cheekbones with a hard lower ridge, a triangular nose bridge and heavy tip, a snarling lip, carved wrinkles and frown lines, swept-back horns, curved bone fangs.
- **Beast-face pauldron:** the mane was sausage-like blobs; it is now flame tongues with a flat outer face, in two layers, plus a back ruff. The saber's resting channel is still clear: in kael.idle the blade lies on the coat at the shoulder beside the pauldron.
- **Mesher bug (the main fix):** the meshes made from distance fields came out with their faces pointing inward. The ambient-occlusion bake therefore came out completely black, and the normal map was inverted. That is what made the mask and pauldron look like dark broken chrome in the engine. One line in `kael_lib.sdf_mesh` fixes it; the occlusion map is now about 0.48 on average instead of 0.
- **Bake helper:** `KL.bake_maps_clean` hides the low-poly mesh from rays while baking. It is defensive only: the tests showed the normals were the actual fault, but I kept it.
- **Other look work:**
  - Three raised sword scars on the chest and belly.
  - The face scarf is now rust-red with overlapping wrapped bands; it was a plain black hood.
  - The loose mane has more and wider locks (39 instead of 30).
  - The crack glow is cut to a few thin cracks with fainter hot patches; before, it washed over both iron pieces.
  - The verdigris on the bronze is damped so no teal shows.
  - The iron is rougher, and the hard pieces get a dimmer, tighter rim light; the old rim made white streaks along every ridge.
  - A `LOOKS` hook in design.js lets materials be retuned in JS without re-running Blender.
- **Budget:** decimation targets lowered to bring the asset under 60k (it was 61,941).
- **README:** the hero README has a new Look section (parts, materials, glow channels, cloth and spring bones, how to rebuild, numbers, known issues).

**Numbers (high tier, this machine):**

| | Kael | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| Triangles | 59,621 | ≤ 60k |
| Draw calls | 4 (gear, cloth, hair, blade) | ≤ 6 |
| Asset size | 2.12 MB (1.59 MB geometry, 0.54 MB maps) | ≤ 2.2 MB |
| Boot | header 1.4 ms, parts 15–19 ms, second Kael 49 ms | ≤ 150 ms |
| char.update median / p90 | 0.3–0.4 / ≤ 0.7 ms (idle, walk, light1) | ≤ 1 ms |
| Low tier char.update | 0.3 ms | |

- The first Kael on a page takes about 600 ms. I believe most of that is the kit's one-time texture generation (same pattern as the pilot), but I did not split it out.
- Three create/dispose cycles leave geometries, textures and programs unchanged.
- A full rebuild takes about 2.5 minutes with one Blender process at a time.

**Review:**
- **Lab captures:** turntable, bust, chest, hands on the grip, idle shoulder, silhouette line-up and the arena line-up. Kael is unmistakable next to the other two: broad, with the saber on his shoulder.
- **Lab clip sheets, 6 frames each:** idle, walkF, dash, guard, light1, sweep, eruption, pyre, hitHeavy. At those camera distances shoulders, elbows, hips and knees deform cleanly, and the cloth, mane and sash don't visibly pass through the body or the saber.
- **Private game build** (training mode against Iska): idle, light1, heavy, skill1, the ultimate opener, and a heavy hit taken from Iska all render without page errors.
- **Not captured as their own sheets:** dash, walk and guard in the game itself (only in the lab), and a knockdown.

result.summary:
VORN (뇌진천 雷震天) now wears a Blender-built model in the game, starting from the pilot. It uses 58,702 triangles and 4 draw calls, and the asset is 1.73 MB. `char.update` is 0.5 ms median / 0.7 ms p90 on high and 0.3 / 0.4 ms on low. The dispose check is clean, and the private game build is 9.8 MB. All of these are within budget.

No earlier VORN work existed, so I started from the pilot. The rig is untouched where the clips depend on it: an export before and after my change shows identical proportions, sockets (visor, hornR, hornL, finL, runes), weapon extent (-0.975 to 1.5), grips and core bones. The only rig additions are three spring chains (queue1..4, wrapTail1..2, tassel1..2) and the three skirt cloth panels, which bring back the default head/neck capsules exactly as the old surcoat did.

**What he wears:**
- **Hat:** a deep conical bamboo hat (radius 0.30 m, height 0.32 m). A real over-under plait was modelled and baked into normal / AO maps on a low cone, with a dark lining, an inner crown so it sits on the head, a bound double rim, a bronze finial and chin cords.
- **Face and hair:** a smoke-violet face wrap with horizontal folds, a knot at the nape and two tails on spring bones; eyes that glow violet-white under the brim; a braided queue on spring bones.
- **Robe:** storm-violet silk with crossed ink-black collars, a pale inner collar strip and old-gold thunder-pattern brocade. Brocade also runs on the cuffs, the cuirass's top binding and the skirt hem bands.
- **Armour:** a black lacquered lamellar cuirass and left shoulder piece laced in old gold, and a lamellar waist guard.
- **Lower body and limbs:** a black hemp sash with a tied knot; a three-panel split skirt draped by Blender cloth and bound to the game's cloth panels; trousers gathered into tall wrapped boots with leather garters; bound forearms and palms.
- **Spear (뇌룡창), exactly the old length and grips:** a leaf head with a raised midrib and honed bevels, a lightning bolt inlaid on both flats that lights up when the move effects flare the inlay channel, bronze socket, crossguard, bands and butt cap, lacquered shaft, two violet grip wraps, and a violet horsehair tassel on its own spring chain.

**Glow:** the eyes, the spear bolt (inlay), and the brocade thread plus gold lacing (vein) all respond to `char.glow`, and the existing storm crackle (`glow.crackle`) is kept. `attach()` binds the hat's baked maps and skips them on the low tier.

**Review captures:** I captured the Blender sheets and, in the real renderer, a turntable, full figure, bust, face, waist, back, a silhouette line-up and a lit line-up. In a private game build (`#training=vorn,iska`) I captured idle, walk, dash, guard, light (flash_jab), heavy (gale_sweep), skill (thunder_javelin), the ultimate opener (ninefold_storm), hit and knockdown, 6 frames each. There were no page errors.

Fixes made along the way:
- Look materials were being deleted by the memory cleanup step before they were assigned to anything.
- The waist guard's surface wrapped around the open back, which put plates sticking out behind the hips.
- The face wrap read as a black void under the hat; I lightened it so its folds show.
- The lacquer plates threw bloom stars; I made them rougher.

The face wrap and lacquer changes are look overrides in `design.js` (`LOOKS`), so they apply without rerunning Blender.

**Timing:** a full Blender build takes about 55 s. Header decode is 1.1 ms and part decode 14–16 ms. A second VORN builds in 37–49 ms. The first VORN takes 470–535 ms; the pilot report attributes this to the kit's one-time texture generation, but I did not measure the split.

Rebuild with `tools/blender/build_assets.sh vorn --preview`. The README covers the parts, materials, glow channels, cloth, springs and these numbers.

New helpers live in `vorn.py` only, not in edlib: `brocade_uvw`, `band_ring` (embroidered limb rings), and fake users on the look materials so the cleanup step can't delete them. That last one is worth adding to edlib; it bit me on the first run.
issues: src/labs/vorn_asset.js is a new file outside my ownership list. It is a copy of the ISKA artist's lab with VORN as the subject, and I made it so my captures would not race the other artists' builds of the shared art lab.

Weapon, grips, sockets and core bones are unchanged (verified by diffing the rig export). The old knight's cloth panels (surcoatF / tailL / tailR particle bones) are replaced by skirtF / skirtBL / skirtBR. The head and neck default colliders are re-added automatically, which logs the same warning as before.

The game review froze each state clip at successive times with game.pose rather than playing the state machine, so hit and down show the clip poses without the real knockback travel. At fight-camera scale the frames show no visible clipping, but no frame-by-frame close-up review of deformation at the joints was done.

result.summary:
I reviewed all three heroes side by side in the lab, the arena and a private game build, and fixed the most visible fault in the roster. The demon mask and beast pauldron on KAEL looked like broken black chrome, and ISKA's silver mask glared. The cause was not their materials or models but a bug in the runtime's baked-map lookup (`src/char/assets.js`). It is fixed, and both masks and the pauldron now read as matte forged iron and engraved silver. I also retuned colours and materials in the design files (no Blender rebuild): VORN's lavender silk is now a deep storm violet, KAEL's grey mane is ink black, and KAEL's skin is darker. Budgets did not change, the dispose check is clean and the private game page is 9.55 MB.

**What I reviewed** (all under `shots/blender/review/`):
- **Lab:** the black-silhouette line-up, the lit roster, the arena line-up and all three arena duels. Also busts, backs, faces and hands for each hero.
- **Private game build** (`build/bl-review.html`, never dist/): a `#demo` match for each pairing (6 frames each), each hero's ultimate (13 frames each), a K.O. sequence, and two `q=low` matches.
- **Verdict:** in pure black the three silhouettes are instantly distinct (heavy saber on the shoulder, slender with twin crescents, tall under the cone hat with the spear). At fight distance they read as murim and grim, with no shimmer and the glow reading as inner energy.

**Fixes:**
1. **Chrome streaks on baked parts (main fix).** UV unwrapping cuts seams through smooth surfaces, so several asset vertices share one position and normal. `attachAssetMaps` matched vertices by position and normal and kept only one entry per position. So one side of every seam took its texture coordinates from the wrong part of the map, which drew bright streaks along every ridge. Turning the maps off made them vanish, which is how I found it. Duplicates are now queued in addAsset and handed out in the merged mesh's order (`src/char/assets.js`). VORN's hat bake never showed it because its UVs have no such seams. This is a runtime fix, so no Blender rebuild was needed.
2. **KAEL** (`src/fighters/kael/design.js`):
   - Fire-blackened matte iron (rougher, less metallic, less edge wear, a dark bare-metal edge colour, a weaker polish lobe).
   - The mane is ink black (it read silver-grey).
   - Darker, weathered skin and a brighter rust-red face scarf.
   - In the game, `attach(char)` now works out the quality tier itself, so the low tier skips KAEL's baked maps there too (ISKA and VORN already did this).
3. **VORN** (`src/fighters/vorn/design.js`): the robe and skirt silk is now a deep dusky violet with less shine. The horsehair tassel and grip wraps follow. The eye band under the hat no longer has a wet sheen.

**Numbers** (high tier, art lab):

| | KAEL | ISKA | VORN | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Triangles | 59,621 | 59,390 | 58,702 | ≤ 60k |
| Draw calls | 4 | 4 | 4 | ≤ 6 |
| `char.update` median | 0.39 ms | 0.47 ms | 0.58 ms | ≤ 1 ms |

- **Asset sizes:** 2.12 / 1.58 / 1.73 MB, unchanged because no asset was rebuilt.
- **Dispose:** clean (12 / 22 / 17). The first ISKA and VORN cycles can show their baked textures being uploaded once; repeated cycles stay flat.
- **Page errors:** none in the lab or game captures.

**READMEs:** the three hero READMEs have a new roster-review section with the changes and numbers, and `tools/blender/README.md` section 8 describes the seam bug and a quick way to diagnose it.
issues: The seam fix assumes the kit's merge keeps each asset part's vertex order. It does today (`build.js`, read-only). If that ever changes, the baked maps would shift again; a rig-team change letting kit pieces carry an extra vertex attribute would remove the lookup entirely.

Up close the hands are still the stock `ed.hand()` mitts. VORN's look like paddles on the spear haft and ISKA's are blocky under the wrap. A sculpted gripping hand in `tools/blender/ed/body.py` (a shared rebuild of all three heroes) is the next step; I did not attempt it.

ISKA's white robe is a smooth, tight shell in the bust (few folds; the sleeves hug the arm rather than float, against MURIM's 'floating sleeves'). Her gauze veil covers the whole lower face as a blue net. Fixing either needs a rebuild of `tools/blender/heroes/iska.py`.
VORN's face under the hat reads as a black, featureless head with a sheen line, and his face wrap is hard to see in the hat's shadow. It is fine at fight distance.

KAEL's face scarf still reads as a near-black hood after the brighter colour. The darkening probably comes from the baked shading and decimation, and its edge at the neck is jagged. That needs a fix in `tools/blender/heroes/kael.py`.
The lab's cool lights still make VORN's violet skirt look bluer than in the arena. In the game it reads as dark storm violet.
Not re-captured: the game's walk, dash and guard as their own sheets (they appear inside the demo frames), and the RPG mode.
